messages:
ben: Heads up — after the kernel rebase on the us-west-2 Ampere pool we're seeing P2P flapping and what looks like BAR1 'shrink' on ~12/120 nodes. Symptoms: NCCL hangs, some jobs fall back to socket, massive perf regression.

alice: Which kernel + driver versions were rolled?

ben: Rolling was kernel 6.1.34 -> 6.1.44 and NVIDIA driver packaged bumped 535.86 -> 535.104. Canary showed a few nodes weirdly affected so we rolled cluster-wide.

carlos: Can you paste the minimal dmesg/pci output from an affected node?

ben: sure, here's the relevant bits from one node (redacted):

```
[  +1.234567] nvidia 0000:af:00.0: BAR1: original 0x40000000 size 0x10000000, now mapped 0x1000000
[  +1.235678] pci 0000:af:00.0: BAR1 size changed; disabling peer-to-peer
[  +1.236789] nvidia 0000:af:00.0: P2P: link state: disabled
[  +1.237890] nv_peer_mem: failed to register peer mapping
[  +1.240000] nvidia: init: PCIe ACS disabled or errata - using fallback
```

lspci -vvv snippet shows ACS flags absent on the bridge.

```
04:00.0 PCI bridge: NVIDIA Device 10fb (rev a1)
	Capabilities: [xx] Express (v3) Endpoint, MSI
	BridgeCtl: Parity+ SERR+ NoACS
```

dana: The kernel rebase included a pci subsystem change (ACS handling) and the distro packaged driver added a small PCI probe tweak. Might be an ordering/timing regression causing BAR probing to re-evaluate sizes.

ben: On affected nodes `nvidia-smi topo -p2p` shows lots of 'X' (no P2P) between GPUs that used to be local. Jobs with NCCL stall trying to use P2P.

carlos: Two quick mitigations: 1) set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 for impacted jobs to force socket fallback (works but slows 3–4x). 2) Roll back driver+kernel on a canary to confirm.

evan: Can we hotfix via kernel cmdline or sysfs to re-enable BAR1/ACS? Any known toggles?

dana: There's no safe runtime toggle for BAR1 size once the device is probed. ACS is set at boot; some vendors have ACS quirks/bios toggles. We can try a heavy probe/unbind/bind cycle but it's risky in prod.

ben: We tried unbind/bind for the GPU and vfio rebind on one node — BAR1 stayed shrunken and P2P remained disabled.

carlos: OK. Plan: immediate → add a cluster-level job label to force affected queues to run with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`. Short term perf hit, but keeps jobs running. Medium → rollback to the previous kernel+driver in the next maintenance window for the whole pool. Long → bisection to find the exact PCI/kernel/driver change.

ben: I created infra ticket INFRA-3287 and a canary rollback job. Canaries already show driver rollback to 535.86 + kernel 6.1.34 restores P2P and BAR1 mapping on the node we tested.

alice: Good. We should also notify product teams — this will affect long-running training jobs.

ben: Notified #customer-impact and put a short status note on the console.

deploybot: Scheduled rollback of driver package on 12 nodes (canary set) at 2027-02-18T22:30Z — job id deploy-ampere-rollback-17985.

dana: After rollback confirmation we'll do a bisection: try kernel 6.1.44 with old driver; old kernel with new driver; and then identify the minimal repro. Might be a kernel PCIe ordering change that exposes a driver probe race.

carlos: Also check BIOS microcode on affected nodes — vendor released a microcode in the last month that changed ACS capability bits before. Could be an interaction.

ben: Agree. Next steps: 1) throttle workloads and set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE in affected clusters (done). 2) run canary rollback and validate. 3) start bisection + collect raw pci/resource maps on affected vs unaffected nodes.

alice: Thanks — keep updates in this thread. If rollback canary succeeds, escalate to urgent change window. :eyes:

ben: Will update after the canary run (ETA ~30m). :thumbsup:
